findings: only 10 tiles on the BRACS side, so these ratios describe a couple of slides rather than a dataset. Read them as a direction, not a measurement.

the ratio is close to constant at 0.60x across the ladder, so this is a stain-STRENGTH difference and a monotone correction fixes it. It sits OUTSIDE approach 1's alpha jitter (0.8, 1.25), so the model would extrapolate on every BRACS tile. Either widen alpha or train with `standardise=True`, which divides each tile by its own p99 and removes a pure scale difference by construction.
only 9 tiles on the BCSS side, so these ratios describe a couple of slides rather than a dataset. Read them as a direction, not a measurement.

the BRACS/BCSS density ratio runs from 0.73 to 1.25 across the quantile ladder - a 1.7x spread. That is a difference in the SHAPE of the density distribution, not its strength, and no monotone correction removes it: not stain normalisation, not a per-slide white point, not the alpha jitter. Approach 1's `gamma` term is the knob that moves shape, and its training range of 0.5 to 3.5 is what would have to cover this.

the ratio is close to constant at 0.97x across the ladder, so this is a stain-STRENGTH difference and a monotone correction fixes it. It sits inside approach 1's alpha jitter (0.8, 1.25), so the existing augmentation already covers it and nothing need change.

headline.caveat: This is a count of tiles, not of correct tiles. Every BRACS label here is BEETLE's opinion of a region no pathologist has reviewed, so the ceiling on their accuracy is BEETLE's own external non-invasive Dice. A held-out set built from these tiles measures agreement with BEETLE, not with the truth - the only honest test of the trained model is BCSS's real class 1 tiles, kept entirely out of training.
